name: Guanidinoacetate methyltransferase deficiency
aliases: creatine deficiency due to GAMT deficiency

clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive cerebral creatine deficiency syndrome caused by deficiency of guanidinoacetate methyltransferase, the enzyme that methylates guanidinoacetate to creatine
The dual problem is cerebral creatine depletion plus accumulation of neurotoxic guanidinoacetate, which distinguishes it from the pure creatine deficiency of AGAT deficiency
Typically presents in infancy or early childhood with global developmental delay, intellectual disability and often treatment-resistant epilepsy
A movement disorder with extrapyramidal features such as dystonia and dyskinesia, and autistic behaviour, are common
Brain proton MR spectroscopy shows an absent or greatly reduced creatine peak, and MRI may show globus pallidus signal change
Elevated guanidinoacetate in plasma and urine is the key screening abnormality and underlies inclusion in some newborn screening programmes
It is one of the treatable causes of intellectual disability, so early recognition matters
Management is generic: creatine supplementation to replete the brain, dietary arginine restriction and ornithine supplementation to lower guanidinoacetate production
reference.pathophysiology: Creatine is synthesised in two steps: arginine and glycine form guanidinoacetate, which is then methylated by guanidinoacetate methyltransferase to creatine using S-adenosylmethionine. In GAMT deficiency this final step fails, so brain and muscle creatine and phosphocreatine, essential for energy buffering, become depleted, while the precursor guanidinoacetate accumulates. Guanidinoacetate is neurotoxic and epileptogenic, and its build-up together with cerebral creatine deficiency produces the encephalopathy, epilepsy and movement disorder. Treatment aims both to restore creatine and to suppress guanidinoacetate synthesis by limiting arginine and providing ornithine.
additionalDifferentials: Mitochondrial disorders presenting with regression and movement disorder
Primary dystonia and other movement disorder syndromes
Autism spectrum disorder with intellectual disability of undetermined cause
additionalInvestigations: Plasma and urinary guanidinoacetate (elevated) and creatine/creatinine
Brain proton MR spectroscopy for the creatine peak
Brain MRI for globus pallidus signal abnormality
Enzyme activity or functional studies in fibroblasts where available
Electroencephalography to characterise the seizure disorder
redFlags: Refractory epilepsy in a child with unexplained developmental delay
Regression or plateauing of development suggesting an untreated metabolic cause
An absent creatine peak on MR spectroscopy
reference.prognosis: Outcome depends heavily on timing; presymptomatic or early treatment can allow near-normal development, whereas delayed diagnosis often leaves fixed intellectual disability, though seizures and movement symptoms may still improve.
pitfalls: Failing to consider a treatable creatine disorder in a child with unexplained delay and epilepsy
Confusing it with SLC6A8 creatine transporter deficiency, which is not corrected by oral creatine
Not measuring guanidinoacetate, which distinguishes GAMT from AGAT deficiency
Providing creatine alone without arginine restriction and ornithine to control guanidinoacetate
Overlooking normal serum creatinine, which does not exclude cerebral creatine deficiency
references: Stockler-Ipsiroglu S et al. Guanidinoacetate methyltransferase deficiency
Blau N. Physician's Guide to the Diagnosis, Treatment, and Follow-up of Inherited Metabolic Diseases
management: Supplement oral creatine monohydrate to replenish depleted cerebral and muscle creatine
Restrict dietary arginine through a protein-controlled diet to reduce synthesis of neurotoxic guanidinoacetate
Supplement ornithine to further suppress guanidinoacetate production
Treat epilepsy with antiseizure medication, recognising that seizures often improve substantially with metabolic treatment
Manage the extrapyramidal movement disorder and provide developmental and rehabilitation support
Monitor plasma and urinary guanidinoacetate and creatine with dietitian-led metabolic follow-up
Offer genetic counselling for autosomal recessive inheritance and screen at-risk siblings, since presymptomatic treatment allows near-normal development
